1757.note: Filter rows by two flag columns. No joins or aggregation needed.

584.note: A NULL referee is never id 2, so handle it with IS NULL instead of = comparisons.
solution: WHERE referee_id IS NULL OR referee_id <> 2;

595.note: One WHERE with an OR: big by area or big by population.

1148.note: Authors read their own articles. DISTINCT removes repeat views, then sort by id.

1683.note: Tweet content longer than 15 characters is invalid. Count characters with LENGTH.

1378.note: LEFT JOIN keeps every employee, even those without a unique id.
solution: LEFT JOIN employeeuni u ON u.id = e.id;

1068.note: Join sales to product to attach product_name, then pick the year and price from sales.
solution: JOIN product p ON p.product_id = s.product_id;

1581.note: LEFT JOIN visits to transactions; visitors with no matching row have NULL transaction_id. COUNT those per customer.
solution: LEFT JOIN transactions t ON t.visit_id = v.visit_id

197.note: Self-join each day with the previous day and compare temperatures.
solution: JOIN weather w2 ON w1.recorddate = w2.recorddate + 1

1661.note: Pivot start and end timestamps per process, subtract, then average per machine.
solution: MAX(CASE WHEN activity_type = 'start' THEN "timestamp" END) AS processing_time

577.note: LEFT JOIN keeps employees with no bonus; keep bonus < 1000 or NULL.
solution: LEFT JOIN bonus b ON b.empid = e.empid
WHERE b.bonus < 1000 OR b.bonus IS NULL;

1280.note: CROSS JOIN students with every subject, then LEFT JOIN exams so missing exams count as 0.
solution: ON e.student_id = s.student_id AND e.subject_name = sub.subject_name

570.note: Group employees by manager, keep managers with 5+ direct reports, then look up their names.

1934.note: LEFT JOIN signups to confirmations, turn actions into 1/0, and average per user.
solution: ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN c.action = 'confirmed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 2) AS confirmation_rate
LEFT JOIN confirmations c ON c.user_id = s.user_id

620.note: Filter odd ids and non-boring descriptions, then sort by rating descending.

1251.note: Join price periods to sales that fall inside them, then compute a weighted average. NULLIF guards division by zero.
solution: AND u.purchase_date BETWEEN p.start_date AND p.end_date

1075.note: Join project assignments to employees, then average experience per project.
solution: JOIN employee e ON e.employee_id = p.employee_id

1633.note: Divide registrations for a contest by total users, multiply by 100, and order by percentage.
solution: ROUND(COUNT(*) * 100.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users), 2) AS percentage

1211.note: Quality is AVG(rating/position); poor percentage counts ratings below 3. Cast to numeric before dividing.
solution: ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN rating < 3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 2) AS poor_query_percentage

1193.note: Format dates to YYYY-MM, group by month and country, and use conditional SUMs for approved totals.
solution: SUM(CASE WHEN state = 'approved' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS approved_count,
SUM(CASE WHEN state = 'approved' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS approved_total_amount

1174.note: Keep each customer's first order, then measure how many of those are immediate. Compare a tuple with IN.
solution: SUM(CASE WHEN order_date = customer_pref_delivery_date THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*), 2

550.note: Find each player's first date, join back to the next day, and divide by all distinct players.
solution: ) f ON f.player_id = a.player_id AND a.event_date = f.first_date + 1;

2356.note: COUNT(DISTINCT subject_id) per teacher, because one teacher can teach a subject in several departments.
solution: SELECT teacher_id, COUNT(DISTINCT subject_id) AS cnt

1141.note: Count distinct users per day inside the 30-day window.
solution: SELECT activity_date AS day, COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) AS active_users
WHERE activity_date BETWEEN DATE '2019-06-28' AND DATE '2019-07-27'

1070.note: Find the first year per product, then join back to keep only that year's sale row.
solution: SELECT s.product_id, s.year AS first_year, s.quantity, s.price
) f ON f.product_id = s.product_id AND f.first_year = s.year;

596.note: Group by class and keep groups with at least five students.

1729.note: Group followers by user and count rows.

619.note: Group numbers, keep single occurrences, then take the max. MAX over no rows returns NULL.

1045.note: A customer qualifies when their distinct purchased products equal the whole product catalog.
solution: HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT product_key) = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM product);

1731.note: Self-join employees to their reports, then count reports and round the average age.
solution: JOIN employees r ON r.reports_to = e.employee_id

1789.note: Keep rows flagged primary, plus employees who belong to exactly one department.

610.note: A triangle needs every pair of sides to sum above the third side.
solution: CASE WHEN x + y > z AND x + z > y AND y + z > x

180.note: Self-join three consecutive log rows and compare their numbers.
solution: JOIN logs l2 ON l2.id = l1.id + 1 AND l2.num = l1.num
JOIN logs l3 ON l3.id = l1.id + 2 AND l3.num = l1.num;

1164.note: For each product pick the latest price on or before 2019-08-16; default to 10 when none exists.
solution: FROM (SELECT DISTINCT product_id FROM products) p;

1204.note: Running SUM of weight ordered by turn; take the last person that keeps the total within 1000.
solution: SELECT person_name, SUM(weight) OVER (ORDER BY turn) AS total_weight

1907.note: Build each salary bucket with conditional SUM, then stack the three rows with UNION ALL.
solution: SUM(CASE WHEN income < 20000 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS accounts_count
SUM(CASE WHEN income BETWEEN 20000 AND 50000 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
SUM(CASE WHEN income > 50000 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)

1978.note: Low salary plus a manager id that no longer exists in the employees table.
solution: AND manager_id NOT IN (SELECT employee_id FROM employees)

626.note: Swap each odd id with the next even id; the last odd id stays in place.
solution: WHEN id % 2 = 1 AND id = (SELECT MAX(id) FROM seat) THEN id

1341.note: Two ranked queries: top reviewer by count, then top movie by average rating in February 2020. UNION ALL the answers.
solution: JOIN users u ON u.user_id = m.user_id
JOIN movies mo ON mo.movie_id = m.movie_id
WHERE m.created_at BETWEEN DATE '2020-02-01' AND DATE '2020-02-29'

1321.note: Aggregate daily revenue, then use a 7-row window SUM and divide by 7 for the moving average.
solution: SELECT visited_on, amount, ROUND(amount / 7.0, 2) AS average_amount
SELECT visited_on, SUM(daily) OVER (ORDER BY visited_on ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS amount

602.note: Union requester and accepter ids, group them, and take the id with the highest count.
solution: SELECT requester_id AS id FROM requestaccepted

585.note: Keep investments whose tiv_2015 is shared and whose (lat, lon) location is unique, then sum tiv_2016.
solution: SELECT tiv_2015 FROM insurance GROUP BY tiv_2015 HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
SELECT lat, lon FROM insurance GROUP BY lat, lon HAVING COUNT(*) = 1

185.note: A salary is top-three in its department when fewer than three distinct higher salaries exist.
solution: SELECT d.name AS Department, e.name AS Employee, e.salary AS Salary
JOIN department d ON d.id = e.departmentid
WHERE e2.departmentid = e.departmentid AND e2.salary > e.salary

1667.note: UPDATE each name: uppercase the first character, lowercase the rest.

1527.note: Match DIAB1 at the start or after a space; use two LIKE patterns.

196.note: DELETE everything except the smallest id for each email.
solution: SELECT MIN(id) FROM person GROUP BY email

176.note: Sort distinct salaries descending and take the second row. A subquery returns NULL when it does not exist.

1484.note: Group by sell date; aggregate distinct products with STRING_AGG and count them.
solution: STRING_AGG(DISTINCT product, ',' ORDER BY product) AS products

1327.note: Join orders to products, keep February 2020, and sum units with a HAVING threshold.
solution: JOIN orders o ON o.product_id = p.product_id
WHERE o.order_date BETWEEN DATE '2020-02-01' AND DATE '2020-02-29'

1517.note: A valid mail starts with a letter and ends with @leetcode.com. A regular expression is the cleanest filter.
